import pandas as pd

# File paths for source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_31/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_31/training_1.csv"

# Load Source 0
# Schema: ['right_index', 'city', 'driver_count', 'type']
# We ignore 'right_index' as it is an index column, so use index_col=0
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)

# Load Source 1
# Schema: ['city', 'date', 'fare', 'ride_id']
# Use index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Transformation plan:
# Target schema: ['type': string, 'city': string, 'fare': float, 'ride_id': float, 'driver_count': integer]
# Source 0 has: city, driver_count, type
# Source 1 has: city, fare, ride_id
# Common column to join on: 'city'
# Join Source 0 and Source 1 on 'city' to get all target columns
# After join, select and reorder columns to match target schema
# Ensure data types match target schema:
#   type: string (already string)
#   city: string (already string)
#   fare: float (convert if needed)
#   ride_id: float (convert if needed)
#   driver_count: integer (convert if needed)

# Perform inner join on 'city' to combine all needed columns
df_merged = pd.merge(df0, df1, on='city', how='inner')

# Select and reorder columns to match target schema
df_target = df_merged[['type', 'city', 'fare', 'ride_id', 'driver_count']]

# Convert data types explicitly
df_target['type'] = df_target['type'].astype(str)
df_target['city'] = df_target['city'].astype(str)
df_target['fare'] = pd.to_numeric(df_target['fare'], errors='coerce').astype(float)
df_target['ride_id'] = pd.to_numeric(df_target['ride_id'], errors='coerce').astype(float)
df_target['driver_count'] = pd.to_numeric(df_target['driver_count'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# Write the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_31/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_31/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_31/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on city (primary key)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Group by type, city, driver_count (leftmost non-float unique columns)
# Aggregate fare and ride_id by mean (to reduce duplicates and match target)
result = joined.groupby(["type", "city", "driver_count"], as_index=False).agg({
    "fare": "mean",
    "ride_id": "mean"
})

# Ensure column order matches target schema
result = result[["type", "city", "fare", "ride_id", "driver_count"]]

# Write output
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_31/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
